author: Akien
prose:
re paths: lets make everything either ${CAIRN_HOME}/whatever like ${CAIRN_HOME}/cairn/devices to differentiate it from CairnCommons which will become ${CAIRN_COMMONS}/whatever and CAIRN_RUNTIME will usually be ~/.cairn/ and it's cairn's job to set it before spawning anything if it's not set. Then we set mine at the bottom of .bashrc -- but there sould also be absolutely no ~/dev/src or /home/akien anywhere in the code or docs or in network (github) artifacts (which means a scrubbing pass. we don't need to scrub it as deeply as they do for enterprise passwords or anything. but shouldn't be in the current code. what do you think?

[on being asked whether the driver was portability]
i almost agree with all of that- the one reason i phrased it the way i did: /home/akien and ~/dev/src are part of this machine's organization. while i'm not needing to scrub it deep, we also dont need to give would be hackers any clues?

[on whether the back-history is worth a rewrite]
i think it's small. but ip addresses, actual disk organization, things like that seem... suboptimal in the repos.

[closing the scope]
yeah, this isn't perfect security, and we will no doubt have to improve it later. but for now, good enough
